content.text:
Here is the draft. Nothing is saved or planned.

```yaml
id: https://joinedcontext.com/models/waste-bins
name: waste-bins
title: Waste bins
description: Public waste containers and the collection routes that serve them.
version: 1.0.0
prefixes:
  linkml: https://w3id.org/linkml/
  wb: https://joinedcontext.com/models/waste-bins/
default_prefix: wb
default_range: string
imports:
  - linkml:types

enums:
  ContainerStatus:
    description: Operational state of a container.
    permissible_values:
      ok:
      full:
      damaged:

classes:
  CollectionRoute:
    description: A route on which waste containers are emptied.
    attributes:
      id:
        identifier: true
        required: true
      name:
        required: true
        description: Name of the route.
      nextRunDate:
        range: date
        required: true
        description: Date of the route's next run.

  WasteContainer:
    description: A public waste container.
    attributes:
      id:
        identifier: true
        required: true
      fillLevel:
        range: float
        required: true
        unit:
          symbol: "%"
        minimum_value: 0
        maximum_value: 100
        description: How full the container is, in percent.
      temperature:
        range: float
        unit:
          ucum_code: Cel
        description: Temperature inside the container, in degrees Celsius.
      status:
        range: ContainerStatus
        required: true
      location:
        required: true
        description: Position of the container as a GeoJSON Point.
      route:
        range: CollectionRoute
        required: true
        multivalued: false
        description: The one collection route this container belongs to.
```

Choices and open points:
- **Route:** `route` is required and single-valued, which gives "exactly one". LinkML can't enforce that a referenced route exists. The platform has to check that.
- **Location:** this is the weakest part. I typed it as a plain string, because LinkML has no native GeoJSON type. The platform may have its own convention for geo properties, such as an NGSI-LD GeoProperty. I'd check that before the plan step, and I can change it to latitude and longitude slots if you prefer.
- **Temperature:** it is optional, since not every container has a sensor. Say so if it should be required.
- **Range on fill level:** I limited `fillLevel` to 0–100.

The manifest would be `waste-bins`, version `1.0.0`, lifecycle `draft`. Do you want me to dry-run it with the plan tool? That still saves nothing.
